description: Signature edition. This entry teaches What Stochastic Processes Studies as part of the fundamentals of stochastic processes, presented the Signature way: from first principles, in plain language, building toward mastery. It sits at the Foundations tier of the teaching ladder, where each idea earns its place before the next is introduced. Signature-authored and Signature-labeled throughout.
overview: In the Signature teaching of stochastic processes, What Stochastic Processes Studies is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Markov chains means memoryless sequences where the future depends only on the present state. Brownian motion means continuous random wiggling, the limit of random walks and model of diffusion. Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Foundations material that follows.
core_concepts: Markov chains: memoryless sequences where the future depends only on the present state.
Brownian motion: continuous random wiggling, the limit of random walks and model of diffusion.
key_laws: Chapman-Kolmogorov equations: multi-step transition probabilities compose by matrix multiplication.
vocabulary: State space: the set of values a process can take.
Hitting time: the random moment a process first reaches a target.
methods: Chain classification: identifying recurrence, periodicity, and absorption.
history: Markov introduced his chains in 1906; Einstein and Wiener formalized Brownian motion. Queuing theory, stochastic calculus, and the Black-Scholes revolution in finance all rest on this foundation.
key_points: Markov chains: memoryless sequences where the future depends only on the present state.
Brownian motion: continuous random wiggling, the limit of random walks and model of diffusion.
